status_vocabulary.resolved: A concrete pinned-engine mapping exists, is implemented here and is checked by a test or by the replay itself.

mappings.decision: Feed timestamps are each row's bar END instant (ts_event_ns) as tz-aware UTC. calendar stays None and enforce_sessions False, so no session filter can drop the 16:00 or 13:00 bars. The declared short session 2019-12-24 (4 rows) is carried from the Nautilus manifest.
mappings.known_short_sessions_reason: 2019-12-24 is the XNYS Christmas Eve half day, closing at 13:00 New York, so it yields the 09:00, 10:00, 11:00 and 12:00 rows only. 104 sessions x 7 rows - 3 missing rows = 725.
evidence: ml4t_backtest-0.1.12 wheel ml4t/backtest/engine.py lines 201-345 (calendar session filtering runs only when a calendar is configured) and 359 (session mode only with a session_col)
ml4t_backtest-0.1.12 wheel ml4t/backtest/datafeed.py lines 297-345 (one feed event per distinct timestamp, in sorted order)
mappings.validation: convert.check_sessions refuses any undeclared short or long session. The port checks that the engine dispatched on_data exactly once for each of the 725 end instants, in order, with skipped_bars 0 and 725 recorded portfolio states.

Bundled history carries no original availability attestation, so event time is preserved but observation time is not independently attested.

mappings.lean_concept: A completed 16:00 bar may form an intent; the fill must land on a later session
mappings.engine_concept: Strategy.on_data at the decision bar's timestamp (its end, 16:00 New York) forms the intent from that completed bar and submits a market order. Under NEXT_BAR an order submitted during a bar is excluded from that bar's processing and first becomes eligible at the next bar's open.
mappings.decision: on_data at the decision bar's timestamp (its end, 16:00 New York) forms the intent from that completed bar. Under NEXT_BAR the order is eligible only at the next bar, which check_decision_bar_is_session_final requires to be the next session's first bar; check_causality runs on the native fills.

ml4t_backtest-0.1.12 wheel ml4t/backtest/core/order_book.py line 86 (an order records the engine clock at submission as created_at)
mappings.validation: fixture_strategy.check_decision_bar_is_session_final at each decision, fixture_strategy.check_causality on the native fills of both runs, and the engine clock at submission (order.created_at) recorded beside each intent and required to be at or after the decision instant and before the fill.
limitations: The guard proves the decision bar was not used to execute. Session-final decision bars are what make the next eligible bar an opening bar; that dependency is recorded under market_on_open_proxy.

mappings.lean_concept: MarketOnOpenOrder filled by EquityFillModel.MarketOnOpenFill at the next session's first hourly bar OPEN, stamped at that bar's end (10:00 New York)
mappings.engine_concept: Ordinary OrderType.MARKET order from on_data under ExecutionMode.NEXT_BAR with ExecutionPrice.OPEN: filled in the next bar's _process_orders(use_open=True) at that bar's open and stamped with that bar's timestamp, the bar end instant.
mappings.decision: An ordinary market order from on_data under NEXT_BAR with execution_price open fills at the next bar's open, stamped with that bar's timestamp (docs/user-guide/execution-semantics.md lines 11-17 and 43-44; engine.py 480-509; execution/fill_executor.py 244). Faithful to LEAN's MarketOnOpenFill only because the decision bar is session-final.
evidence: docs/user-guide/execution-semantics.md lines 11-17 and 43-44 at 672804b36915742fe18af9cd09b44e9839d39d6f
ml4t_backtest-0.1.12 wheel ml4t/backtest/engine.py lines 492-509 (NEXT_BAR: _process_orders(use_open=True) before the strategy callback)
ml4t_backtest-0.1.12 wheel ml4t/backtest/core/fill_engine.py lines 220-241 (fill price from the configured execution_price, open when use_open)
ml4t_backtest-0.1.12 wheel ml4t/backtest/execution/fill_executor.py line 244 (Fill.timestamp is the current bar time)
mappings.validation: The port records each native fill's price, price source and instant and checks that it lands on the next session's first bar at that bar's open (guards fill_at_next_session_first_bar and fill_price_is_fill_bar_open). compare.py compares price and instant against the oracle with zero tolerance.
limitations: Faithful to LEAN's MarketOnOpenFill only because each decision bar is its session's final bar; a decision on an earlier bar would fill at the next hourly bar's open, which is not an opening auction.
The pre-open target-intent contract with OPG time-in-force, documented for daily opening auctions, is not used.
docs/user-guide/profiles.md lines 37-40 scope the lean profile to daily US equities; hourly bars are outside that documented scope and this trial says so.

mappings.lean_concept: Raw-normalized cash dividends posted to the account at the ex-date, derived from the bundled factor file; unexpected splits block the fixture
mappings.engine_concept: Engine(..., funding_df=frame): one row per derived distribution with timestamp = the ex-date session's first converted row (its bar END instant), asset SPY and amount_per_unit = -per_share. The engine posts cash_delta = -quantity * multiplier * amount_per_unit from its own position before the orders eligible at that timestamp and records a FundingPayment, zero when flat.
mappings.decision: Engine-posted through the documented funding input: one funding_df row per derived distribution at the ex-date session's first bar end, amount_per_unit = -per_share; the engine computes cash_delta = -quantity * multiplier * amount_per_unit from its own position (broker.py 458-498; docs/user-guide/market-impact.md lines 229-268). Declared repurposing of a perpetual-futures input and a 10-hour posting-instant difference from LEAN's 00:00 ex-date.

ml4t_backtest-0.1.12 wheel ml4t/backtest/funding.py lines 36-81 (events must match feed timestamps and feed assets)
mappings.validation: engine_posted is true for an event exactly when the engine recorded a FundingPayment for it, and the ledger carries that payment's cash_delta, quantity and timestamp. The port checks one payment per funding row and no other payment, and that the engine's per-bar cash changes only at fills and nonzero payments. compare.py rebuilds the cash path from the receipt and checks the distribution total and the native end cash against the oracle.
limitations: Declared repurposing: the funding input is documented for perpetual futures; its amount_per_unit semantics are a generic per-unit cash flow, which is what a raw-normalized cash dividend is.

Postings land at the ex-date's first bar end, 10:00 New York (1576854000 and 1584712800), not at LEAN's 00:00 ex-date instants (1576818000 and 1584676800). Nothing can fill between 00:00 and that bar, so the eligible quantity is the same; the v1 contract does not compare distribution instants against the oracle.
Bar prices stay raw-normalized. Payable dates, withholding and short-position debits are outside one_zero.

mappings.lean_concept: SecurityMarginModel(2m) with DefaultMarginCallModel, post-processing marks, hourly peak and a one-way 5% drawdown latch
mappings.engine_concept: The lean profile's margin account: allow_short_selling and allow_leverage true, initial, long-maintenance and short-maintenance margin 0.5. Not established as equivalent to LEAN's margin models.
mappings.decision: The lean preset's margin account (allow_leverage, initial and maintenance margin 0.5) is not claimed equivalent to LEAN's SecurityMarginModel(2m) or DefaultMarginCallModel. one_zero requests 1x, so no leverage, margin call or latch is exercised or claimed.

limitations: Equivalence to SecurityMarginModel(2m), DefaultMarginCallModel timing and quantity, the hourly peak and the one-way 5% latch remains undecided and blocks two_zero, two_stress, adaptive_stress and over_limit.
The account type (MARGIN) differs from the Nautilus arm's CASH account; at 1x with no shorting this has no measured effect on one_zero, and no margin-remaining series is compared.
